question: Which experiments have demonstrated heralded entanglement between two remote quantum memories, and what herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time did each report?

Q0.label: main
Q0.text: Which experiments have demonstrated heralded entanglement between two remote quantum memories, and what herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time did each report?
Q0.keywords: heralded entanglement remote quantum memories experiment demonstration herald rate Bell state fidelity storage time

Q1.label: subject
Q1.text: Two spatially separated quantum memory nodes, such as trapped ions, single neutral atoms, atomic ensembles, nitrogen-vacancy or silicon-vacancy centres in diamond, or rare-earth doped crystals, that are linked by photons to form a quantum network.
Q1.keywords: quantum network nodes memory trapped ion neutral atom atomic ensemble nitrogen-vacancy NV silicon-vacancy SiV rare-earth crystal

Q2.label: approach
Q2.text: Heralded entanglement generation by interfering photons emitted by or stored in the two memories and detecting them at a midpoint station, including two-photon Barrett-Kok, single-photon and DLCZ schemes with a Bell-state measurement.
Q2.keywords: heralding photon interference Bell-state measurement two-photon Barrett-Kok single-photon DLCZ midpoint detection spin-photon entanglement

Q3.label: outcome
Q3.text: Reported figures of merit for remote entanglement: the heralding rate or success probability per attempt, the fidelity of the heralded Bell state, and the memory storage or coherence time that limits how long the entanglement is kept.
Q3.keywords: entanglement rate success probability per attempt Bell state fidelity coherence time storage time memory lifetime

Q4.label: context
Q4.text: Memory nodes placed in separate laboratories or buildings and connected by optical fibre over distances from metres to kilometres, possibly with quantum frequency conversion to telecom wavelengths for low-loss transmission.
Q4.keywords: separate laboratories buildings optical fibre kilometres distance metropolitan telecom wavelength frequency conversion
